title: Sunway Serene 2: family-sized lakeside units for rightsizers.
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #418 | SUNWAY SERENE 2, PETALING JAYA
excerpt: Two towers of 993 units and 27 landed homes beside a lake and golf course between the LDP and Federal Highway. Sean likes the location, the step-free design and the listed specs, but notes the traffic and empty industrial land opposite.
takeaways: Units from 995 to 1,590 sq ft, three bedrooms and up, from about RM860,000, around RM870 psf.
Step-free from car park to bathroom, with every material brand listed at launch.
Leasehold, beside a congested shortcut road and an industrial zone with an uncertain future.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Serene 2 is the second phase of a lakeside development: two towers of 993 units plus 27 two- and three-storey landed homes from about RM2.3 million that share the facilities. Each floor has 11 units served by five passenger lifts. Speed ramps take residents straight into the car park, and the deck mixes a resort-style pool with beach entry, lap lanes and an infinity edge over the lake with nature trails, a pickleball court and a senior lounge and exercise corner.

Units run from 995 sq ft to 1,590 sq ft. Sean viewed the 1,590 sq ft four-bedroom corner unit: living and dining laid side by side onto a 21 ft balcony, a dry kitchen divided from the wet kitchen by a glass sliding door, and a wheelchair-friendly junior suite at the front. Every brand, from flooring to air conditioners, is listed at launch.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: The site lies between the LDP and the Federal Highway beside Subang National Golf Club, surrounded by landed homes, so tower views should stay open. Sunway City Kuala Lumpur is close, with two years of shuttle vans provided, and schools, malls and PJ, Subang and Bandar Sunway's food are all nearby. Across the road is the ageing Sungai Way free trade zone, where old factories are being reused.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: Prices start at about RM860,000, around RM870 psf. Sean notes that rents in the first phase would already cover the instalment on a Serene 2 unit, and many buyers are first-phase owners upgrading to bigger units for own stay.

standout.title: A private suite at the front door
standout.body: Next to the entrance sits a bedroom with its own wheelchair-friendly bathroom, set apart from the rest of the home. It suits an elderly parent who wants their own space yet eats dinner with the family, or a home office, without the developer forcing a multi-generation label on the layout.

pros: The location: between the Federal Highway and the LDP, beside a golf course in a low-density landed area that guarantees views, with a mature community and amenities in PJ, Subang and Bandar Sunway.

The project: bigger than the first phase, with resort-style facilities around the towers, design for elderly residents who are rightsizing from old landed homes, and a corner unit with three open sides, a separate dry and wet kitchen, safe aircon ledges and larger windows. Materials are specified up front.
The developer: a township builder that stays for the long term, with shuttles, after-sales maintenance services and its own land nearby, so it won't undercut its earlier phases.
cons: The access road is a shortcut between the LDP and the Federal Highway and gets congested at peak hours, though the developer is building an extra turning lane for residents.
The empty industrial land opposite: he doubts it will become high-rise, and the plot right in front belongs to the developer, but its future is uncertain.
The title is leasehold, which matters to own-stay buyers, though he notes a nearby project was converted to freehold.

closing: A family-sized own-stay home in central PJ for upgraders and rightsizers; Sean's pick is the 1,590 sq ft unit or a landed home.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this December 2025 episode and its video description. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. The developer's team showed Sean the sales gallery, show unit and site; prices are theirs. The land carries a commercial title, which is why the units have sprinklers.
